public_rationale: Part of the claim holds. LLM supply grew fast. Stanford's AI Index counts 149 foundation models released in 2023, over double 2022, and 65.7% were open-source. Weeks after the post, Meta's LLaMA-13B beat GPT-3 on most benchmarks. That fits 'quickly becoming commodities' for older capability levels. But the frontier was not a commodity in 2023. The same AI Index found closed models held a median 24.2% performance edge on 10 benchmarks, and OpenAI's revenue rose to about $80M a month. The IP clause is hedged ('not clear') and is not scored.
limitations: 'Commodity' is undefined in the post, so the result depends on our reading.
The time window (launch through 2023) is our choice; later years (e.g., narrowing open/closed gaps) might read differently.
Summary-level evidence; full report not accessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are quickly becoming commodities, and it is unclear OpenAI has any unique, protectable IP.

statement.excerpt: Meanwhile, large language models themselves are quickly becoming commodities; it’s not clear that there is any unique, protectable intellectual property here.
statement.document_title: Is Microsoft about to get the deal of the century? Or is Sam Altman unloading OpenAI at just the right time?

from_speaker: large language models themselves are quickly becoming commodities
it's not clear that there is any unique, protectable intellectual property here
What can OpenAI do that Google couldn't quickly replicate
our_interpretation: Plain reading of 'quickly becoming commodities': around and soon after the post, many providers were releasing comparable LLMs, so that OpenAI's models were not clearly better or hard to substitute.
Because 'quickly becoming' describes an ongoing process, the target period is ChatGPT's launch through the end of 2023.
The second half ('it's not clear that there is any unique, protectable IP') is hedged and is not scored on its own.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that during 2023 many organizations released LLMs close to OpenAI's in capability, including openly available ones, so OpenAI's models were easily replaced.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that during 2023 OpenAI's or other closed frontier models kept a clear, measurable performance lead that competitors could not quickly replicate.

evidence.excerpt: This past year, organizations released 149 foundation models, more than double the number released in 2022. Of these newly released models, 65.7% were open-source
evidence.explanation: Supply of foundation models more than doubled in 2023 and most were open-source, consistent with LLMs spreading toward commodity status.

evidence.excerpt: Closed-source models still outperform their open-sourced counterparts. On 10 selected benchmarks, closed models achieved a median performance advantage of 24.2%
evidence.locator: section But At a Cost of Performance?
evidence.explanation: In 2023, leading closed models such as OpenAI's kept a large measured lead, so frontier LLMs were not yet interchangeable commodities.

evidence.excerpt: LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 (175B) on most benchmarks, and LLaMA-65B is competitive with the best models, Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B. We release all our models to the research community.
evidence.explanation: Weeks after the post, Meta released models that beat GPT-3 on most benchmarks. This supports quick replication of earlier OpenAI capability by others.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI was currently generating around $80 million a month
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's fast revenue growth in 2023 suggests its products were not yet priced as commodities, but revenue is an indirect measure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A direct cross-vendor comparison of 2023 price and quality, showing whether OpenAI's models could be readily swapped for others at similar cost.
